extraction_text: The text describes the composition of the human body and sensory system according to ancient wisdom.
The body is composed of the five elements: earth, space (ether), fire, wind (air), and water.
The five senses (eyes, nose, ears, skin, tongue) perceive their respective objects (form, smell, taste, touch, sound).
The soul (knower of the field) perceives sensory objects through the senses, not the senses themselves.
The hierarchy of perception: senses < mind < intellect < soul.
Eight perceptual organs: mind, five senses, heart (emotion), and intellect.
Six action organs: hands, feet, anus, genitals, mouth, and physical strength.
Sleep occurs when senses rest from their activities; dreams occur when senses rest but the mind remains active.
Three qualities (gunas) exist: sattva (goodness), rajas (passion), and tamas (ignorance), all connected to action.
A being is composed of 19 components: senses, qualities, etc., plus heat, totaling 20 components.
The soul repeatedly leaves one body and enters another due to karma, like moving from an old house to a new one.
The soul is eternal, neither created nor destroyed, and experiences pleasure and pain alone in the body.
